title: GeoNerd: AI visibility digest for UK accountancy practices

problem_severity_frequency.rationale: Pain is inferred, not evidenced: the argument rests on AIO/YMYL prevalence and a shared-question structure, not on any accountant describing the problem as frequent or costly. Analogy-based problem score is capped at 2 under weights 1.1.0 (assumption A2).

buyer_budget_clarity.rationale: Buyer is precise (owner/partner of a 1-20 staff UK practice). Budget is not demonstrated for this product, but incumbents (TendorAI, SearchScore) already sell AI-visibility tooling to this exact buyer at $25-299/mo, which is affirmative evidence a budget line exists. No observed willingness to pay for GeoNerd itself, so 3 not 4.

evidence_strength.rationale: All evidence is internal desk research: category counts, vendor pricing and published measurement studies. No buyer-derived or independent verification. Category analysis without buyer evidence scores 2 under weights 1.1.0.

distribution.rationale: Channels are plausible (directories, AccountingWEB/ICAEW/ACCA communities, SEO, benchmark report) but no channel has produced a prospect, reply or scan yet (assumption A4). Plausible-only distribution is capped at 2.

differentiation.rationale: TendorAI already markets AI visibility to UK ICAEW/ACCA accountants, SearchScore has audited 1,038 UK accountancy firms and sells tracking from $25/mo, and Tramwai/AireStream contest the services end. Direct incumbent overlap caps differentiation at 2.

validation_speed_cost.rationale: A 1-week, <=GBP50, <=20 human-hour test with a pre-fixed mechanical decision rule (>=2 of 5 practices commit at >=GBP19; >=25% email capture; >=1 non-network channel). Genuinely cheap and decisive for the central assumption.

feasibility.rationale: The manual version of the scan is straightforward and is what the experiment uses. The automated UI-equivalent measurement pipeline (noise, provider cost, caching) is unproven, which caps feasibility at 3.

economics.rationale: Contribution margin is modelled, not measured. It depends on untested density (>=10 customers/market at GBP19.99), untested provider cost and untested support load (assumption A5). Modelled-only economics with untested inputs are capped at 2, low confidence.

founder_fit.rationale: No evidence about the actual founder's access to UK accountancy practices or ability to operate the product. Scored null rather than guessed.

risk.rationale: No regulated data, no personal data beyond an email, and claims can be stated honestly. Main exposure is dependence on third-party AI surfaces and contested positioning, both manageable, neither veto-level.

economic_buyer.note: Owner/partner of a 1-20 staff UK practice owns the problem and controls a marketing/BD budget; the product price is trivial against the value of one new client.

painful_frequent_or_budgeted.note: Pain and urgency are assumed by analogy with search-visibility tracking; no accountant has been observed describing the problem unprompted or paying for a fix (assumption A2). Previously recorded as pass on the strength of an assumption; corrected under weights 1.1.0.
painful_frequent_or_budgeted.resolve_via: geonerd-demand-spike interviews: whether practices raise the problem unprompted, what they currently do about it, and whether >=2 of 5 commit at >=GBP19/mo.

non_paid_distribution.note: Directory outreach, professional communities, SEO and a benchmark report are plausible non-paid channels, but none has produced a scan, reply or conversation yet (assumption A4).
non_paid_distribution.resolve_via: Measure directory-outreach reply and scan-start rates and community-post yield during the spike; >=1 non-network channel producing a conversation resolves it.

defensible_wedge.note: The proposed wedge (vertical depth + honest measurement + plain-language actions) can be described, but TendorAI and SearchScore already contest AI visibility for UK accountants and free checkers cover the generic case. Describable positioning is not evidence of a defensible wedge.
defensible_wedge.resolve_via: Interview reactions to positioning and price against TendorAI/SearchScore and the free checkers; a differentiated job (not price) must be confirmed by buyers.

no_network_effects_needed.note: The market-level prompt set is shared infrastructure; a single practice receives a useful scan and digest without any other customer.

plausible_margins.note: Contribution is modelled positive only at untested density (>=10 customers/market at GBP19.99) with untested UI-equivalent collection cost (assumption A5).
plausible_margins.resolve_via: Record the actual provider bill for the manual/automated scans and the achieved density after the spike; positive contribution at observed density resolves it.

acceptable_risk.note: No regulated data; email is the only personal data; vendors are only cited, not scraped into a product. Third-party surface dependency and incumbent contest are recorded as manageable.

cheap_disconfirming_test.note: A 1-week demand spike with a pre-fixed decision rule can disprove the central assumption (practices commit at >=GBP19/mo) for <=GBP50 and <=20 human-hours.

not_all_optimistic.note: The pre-fixed stop rule kills the idea on 0/5 commitments even if every optimistic reading holds; an iterate path and an API-cost fallback are documented.

review.requested_from: ChatGPT (independent reviewer, routed by the human owner)

history.reason: Bootstrap seed at validation-ready under issue #1; independent review requested because the idea was proposed at an advanced state.
